title: Discerning What Matters: A Multi-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Competence in LLMs
benchmark_measurement: General moral competence across five dimensions (identifying features, weighting importance, assigning reasons, synthesizing judgments, recognizing information gaps). Some of the moral vignettes used for measurement included religious contexts (e.g., religious dietary restrictions, adherence to church teachings) as a situational factor.
findings: Religion was included as a demographic variable for the human participants in both experiments (Christianity, Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, and No Religion were reported). Additionally, some of the moral vignettes used in the evaluation contained religious elements as contextual details (e.g., a character following church teachings, or a community's religious dietary restrictions). However, the paper does not provide a specific analysis of how these religious factors influenced the moral reasoning performance of LLMs or humans.
